   - Why: Delayed appearance after trauma, persistent hemosiderin pigment and fluid signal on MRI; organized hematomas can develop spindle cell/fibrous reaction and incorporate surrounding fat.

   - Why: Occurs in hands/feet, may show mixed cell populations, myxoid change, hemosiderin, and can overlap histologically with HFLT. Important to exclude because management differs (wider excision, oncology follow‑up).
   - Clinical implication: Needs pathologic re‑review, immunostains, and molecular testing; referral to sarcoma center if suspected.

   - Why: Shows mature adipocytes admixed with uniform spindle cells; hemorrhage could account for pigment and heterogeneous MRI signal, though this location is less classic.
   - Clinical implication: Benign; excision is curative.

   - Why: Common in the hand and characteristically pigmented by hemosiderin; histology usually shows multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells (not emphasized in the provided report), so less likely but in differential because of location and pigment.
